sources.title: orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored:q4_K_M - ollama.com
sources.snippet: Ollama build of Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored — an abliterated (refusal-removed) build of Qwen's Qwen3.8-27B, a 27B dense hybrid-attention (Gated DeltaNet linear + full attention) native vision-language model with reasoning, tool-calling, and an MTP speculative-decoding head. Sixteen tags from 2-bit to 8-bit, each with the mmproj vision projector bundled in — nothing extra to fetch. Browse all ...

sources.title: smtek/Qwen3.8-27B - ollama.com
sources.snippet: The K_L builds use the real unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF quants (UD = ultra-dynamic), include the vision projector (mmproj-F16), and enable MTP speculative decoding where VRAM allows.

sources.title: How to Run Qwen 3.8 27B Locally: Ollama, GGUF, and ... - yottalabs.ai
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-27B is out: Apache 2.0, a surprise vision encoder, and 262k context. Which quant fits your VRAM, the Ollama and GGUF routes, and how to be generating tokens today.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-27B Uncensored GGUF: Abliterated Local Build
sources.snippet: Bottom line "Qwen 3.8 27B uncensored GGUF" has an answer, and it is a concrete download: Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GGUF — F16 plus 12 quantization tiers for llama.cpp, the abliterated weights from our FP8 build, 262K context, vision, and MTP, under Apache 2.0 and research-only.

sources.title: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF · The model is really slow due to unclear reason
sources.snippet: I tested quantizations UD-Q4_K_XL and Q4_K_M on CMP 50HX (upgraded to 20GB VRAM) with llama.cpp b10434. No matter of context size, KV-cache quantization, enabled/disabled MTP: performance always is around 7-10 t/s.
